corrected_recommendation:
Keep Part A (with four corrections) and keep B1/B4/B5/B6/B7/B9. Retract the headline verdict "works-native-fast / adds approximately 0 ms" and retract the stated insertion points for B2, B3 and B8.

Corrected framing:

1. B8 (retrieval grounding) is NOT free and NOT off the critical path in this architecture. The upstream speech-to-speech process owns turn triggering and prompt assembly; the orchestrator sees the user transcript only after the response is already generating (its only remedy at that point is response.cancel, orchestrator.py:511-521). Grounding a turn therefore requires one of: (a) cancel + inject conversation.item.create + response.create, which adds a full extra LLM round trip and will not fit the 2.0 s budget as an afterthought; (b) accept one-turn-late grounding, which is useless; or (c) patch the upstream pipeline. Pick (a) and re-budget the turn, or (c) and scope the fork. Do not ship the plan's "<=50 ms, concurrent with prompt assembly" claim.

2. Re-point B3 at voxemw/gateway/audio_pacer.py:54 (AudioPacer.feed_audio, called from orchestrator.py:610). That is the single unavoidable in-repo chokepoint for every synthesized sample. The PCM there is already int16 bytes at 16 kHz mono, so "right before int16 conversion" does not exist in-repo — you de-quantize to float, watermark, re-quantize. Buffers there are sentence-sized (stream_batch_sentences: 1), comfortably above AudioSeal's ~1 s detection floor; the plan's "~240 ms chunk" latency model is wrong (the RTC track consumes 20 ms ticks from the pacer, it does not receive TTS chunks).

3. Re-point B2 at pacer.feed_audio too. _apply_persona (orchestrator.py:343-347) has no audio path — it only sends a websocket session.update — and it fires on every persona swap, not once per session. Critically, pacer.flush() on barge-in (orchestrator.py:604) discards queued audio, so a user who speaks over the disclosure cancels it. Either play the disclosure outside the pacer, or gate flush() until the disclosure has drained. A disclosure the user can silence by talking is not a control.

4. Fix Part A: (i) trim to a temp file FIRST, then run both loudnorm passes on that file — the plan's A3 measures untrimmed audio and A4 applies those numbers to trimmed audio (I measured 0.18 dB drift); (ii) delete the "VERIFIED end-to-end ... 16000 Hz" annotation under A4 — the command says -ar 24000 and the plan's own cited Qwen3-TTS source requires >=24 kHz reference audio, so the annotation, if trusted, produces an out-of-spec reference; (iii) align A1's silencedetect noise=-40dB (peak) with A4's start_threshold=-45dB:detection=rms or the surveyed boundaries won't match what gets cut; (iv) loosen A2's "reject if Flat factor > 0" — any digital-silence padding trips it.

5. Promote "move the LLM local" from a B5 bullet to a precondition. In the default config every turn ships the guardrail preamble, the persona, the user's speech transcript and (if B8 is built) the retrieved dossier to api.deepseek.com. "Local-only is already true by construction" is false for the shipped config, and a third-party model may also refuse or distort content about a recently assassinated US political figure — a functional risk, not only a privacy one.

6. Fix AB 1836's date to January 1, 2025 (leginfo shows approval 2024-09-17 with no delayed-operative clause), and note that secondary sources conflict.

Everything else in the plan survived verification and should be kept as written, including the B6 GUARDRAIL_PREAMBLE fix, which is correct and trivially implementable at orchestrator.py:77.

problems.problem: B8 (retrieval grounding) is architecturally infeasible as specified, and the plan calls it mandatory. It budgets "<=50 ms, fired on the ASR text concurrently with prompt assembly, off the critical path." But the orchestrator does not assemble the prompt — the upstream speech-to-speech process does, and it auto-creates the response on VAD end-of-turn. Grounding requires cancel + re-create (a full extra LLM round trip, blowing the 2.0 s budget), or lands one turn late, or requires forking upstream. Since the plan's own risk list says an ungrounded build is "a fabrication engine" and grounding is "NOT optional," the central verdict "works-native-fast, adds approximately 0 ms" does not hold.
problems.evidence: Verified in ./ref-VoxEMW/voxemw/gateway/orchestrator.py. At line 510 the handler for `conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed` responds to a bad turn by sending `{"type": "response.cancel"}` (lines 515, 522) — the response is already in flight when the transcript arrives. `response.create` is sent by the orchestrator in only two places (:378 vision-tool path, :568), never for a normal turn; line 375's comment ("它的上下文已含上面的工具结果，再发 response.create 会冲突") confirms the upstream process owns normal turn creation. voxemw/pipeline/args.py:34 render_s2s_argv + launch.py:131 confirm the LLM/TTS run in a separate CLI process.

problems.problem: A4's "VERIFIED end-to-end" annotation contradicts the command it annotates, and the contradiction points at an out-of-spec reference file. The command block writes `-ar 24000 ... ref.wav`; the parenthetical directly beneath claims verification produced "pcm_s16le / 16000 Hz / 1 ch." A builder who trusts the annotation over the command ships a 16 kHz reference, below the >=24 kHz minimum stated by the plan's own cited Qwen3-TTS source.
problems.evidence: I ran the A4 chain verbatim: output was sample_rate=24000, channels=1, codec_name=pcm_s16le, duration=12.656625 — so the command is correct and the annotation is false. Fetched https://ocdevel.com/blog/20260302-qwen-tts-voice-cloning (page exists): "Audio must be at least 24 kHz." Separately, configs/assistant.yaml:60 `sample_rate: 16000  # 管线全程 16kHz，勿改` sits under the `tts:` block and is the OUTPUT rate, not the reference rate — the plan conflates the two in B3 ("expects 16 kHz, which is EXACTLY the pipeline rate, so it drops in with no resampling").

problems.problem: B3's named insertion point does not exist in this repository. "Apply in the TTS handler's chunk loop right before int16 conversion" describes code inside the upstream speech-to-speech package, not voxemw/. As stated, B3 is an unscoped upstream fork, not a local edit. The latency model attached to it is also wrong.
problems.evidence: Verified: TTS is launched as a separate process via render_s2s_argv (voxemw/pipeline/args.py:34, called at voxemw/pipeline/launch.py:131). Audio returns over websocket already as int16 PCM and enters the repo at orchestrator.py:610 `self.pacer.feed_audio(pcm)` -> audio_pacer.py:54 `feed_audio(self, pcm: bytes)` docstring "TTS PCM（int16 16k mono）". The RTC track pulls 20 ms / 320-sample ticks (audio_pacer.py:78 `next_audio_tick`, rtc.py:65-67), so the plan's "~240 ms streaming chunk" figure corresponds to nothing in this pipeline.

problems.problem: B2's spoken disclosure is pointed at a function with no audio path, fires on the wrong event, and is defeatable by the user simply talking. This is the one guardrail whose entire job is to be un-defeatable.
problems.evidence: orchestrator.py:343-347 `_apply_persona` body is only `await self.s2s.send(json.dumps(build_session_update(...)))` — no pacer call, no audio. It is invoked on every persona swap (orchestrator.py:479) as well as at :290, so it is not "once per session, ~3 s." And orchestrator.py:604 `self.pacer.flush()` on barge-in clears the queue (audio_pacer.py:65 `self._audio.clear()`), so audio fed through the pacer — including a disclosure — is discarded the moment the user speaks.

problems.problem: The plan understates the cloud LLM. It asserts local-only is "already true by construction" and lists "move the LLM local" as one of five B5 bullets. In the shipped config every turn sends the guardrail preamble, the full persona text, the user's speech transcript and (if B8 is built) the retrieved dossier about a real deceased person to a third-party API. There is also an unflagged functional risk that the model refuses or distorts this subject matter.
problems.evidence: configs/assistant.yaml:40-43 `backend: chat-completions / model_name: deepseek-v4-flash / base_url: https://api.deepseek.com`. Confirmed by grep that this is the only outbound host, which is the plan's own finding — but it is the host that receives the sensitive payload. orchestrator.py:77 `"instructions": persona_text` is what gets sent there.

problems.problem: B5's stated grep evidence is factually wrong. The plan claims web/ "returns ZERO matches" for download|share|upload|export|blob:|a.href. It returns two. The substantive conclusion (no export path) still holds, but the plan's credibility rests explicitly on "I tested this rather than guessed," and one of the tests is misreported.
problems.evidence: grep -rn -iE 'download|share|upload|export|blob:|a\.href|createObjectURL|MediaRecorder|toBlob' web/ returns web/assistant.js:57 (a comment about MediaRecorder forcing decode) and web/assistant.js:203 `URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([WORKLET_SRC], ...))`. The second is the AudioWorklet source blob, not an export; the first shows browser-side recording was previously explored, which is directly relevant to B7.

problems.problem: A3 measures loudness on the untrimmed window but A4 applies silenceremove BEFORE loudnorm, so the measured_* values describe different audio than pass 2 processes. The result misses the stated target and, on a hotter source, risks loudnorm silently falling back to dynamic mode — which would apply exactly the dynamics compression A2 tells you to reject source material for.
problems.evidence: I ran A3 then A4 on a 14.20 s test file (0.5 s silence + 5 s tone + 1.5 s gap + 6 s tone + 1.2 s silence). Pass 1 reported input_i=-32.69. Re-measuring the rendered output gave input_i=-22.82 against the -23 target — 0.18 dB drift attributable solely to the measure/render mismatch. Fix: write the trimmed segment to a temp WAV first, then run both loudnorm passes against that file.

problems.problem: A1 and A4 use mismatched thresholds and mismatched detectors, so the pause boundaries the survey step reports are not the boundaries the render step cuts on — undermining the stated purpose of A1 ("so you cut on silence, never mid-word").
problems.evidence: A1: `silencedetect=noise=-40dB:d=0.35` (silencedetect is peak-based by default). A4: `silenceremove=...start_threshold=-45dB:detection=rms`. Different level and different detector. Also A2's rule "REJECT if Flat factor > 0" is too strict as written — astats reports flat factor for any run of identical samples, so ordinary digital-silence padding or a noise-gated podcast trips it.

problems.problem: California AB 1836's effective date is stated as January 1, 2026. The bill was approved 2024-09-17 and carries no delayed-operative clause, which under California's default rule makes it effective January 1, 2025.
problems.evidence: Fetched https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billNavClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240AB1836 — approved by the Governor September 17, 2024; the bill text specifies no operative or effective date, which per California law means effective January 1 following enactment. Secondary sources do conflict on this point, so the plan is not alone in the error, but the primary source resolves it.

problems.problem: The persona hot-swap hazard is overstated as "a live bug-shaped hazard, not a theoretical one." The websocket handler validates the id against the configured persona set, so a browser can only swap among personas the user themselves configured. The B6 fix is still correct and worth doing; the threat description is not.
problems.evidence: orchestrator.py:476-480: `if event.get("type") == "vox.persona": pid = event.get("id"); if pid in self.personas: await self._apply_persona(pid)`. Unknown ids are silently ignored, not applied.

problems.problem: AudioSeal's maintenance status is thinner than implied. The plan treats it as the safe, maintained default; it has had no release in roughly nine months, and the plan's own cited macOS silent-failure incident is the most recent notable event in its downstream history.
problems.evidence: PyPI JSON for audioseal: latest version is 0.2.0, released 2025-12-17 (today is 2026-09-09). MIT, requires_python >=3.8, files are audioseal-0.2.0-py3-none-any.whl and the sdist; depends on torch>=1.13.0. Pinning to 0.2.0 as the plan recommends is right, but it is pinning to the only version there is.

problems.problem: Nothing in the plan sits between the LLM's text output and the cloned voice. Every guardrail (B1, B2, B6, B8) is upstream of the LLM or outside the audio path; B3/B4 label the audio after the fact. If the LLM complies with a jailbreak or the dossier retrieval returns nothing, the cloned voice speaks the result unconditionally. Because the LLM and TTS share the upstream process, there is no in-repo point to inspect the text before it is spoken.
problems.evidence: The orchestrator relays s2s events and receives `response.output_audio_transcript.delta` (orchestrator.py:533) concurrently with the PCM it feeds to the pacer (:610) — the transcript arrives as deltas alongside audio that is already generated, not before it. The only pre-speech intervention the code demonstrates is `response.cancel` (:515, :522), which kills the whole turn.

surviving_claims: ffmpeg 8.0.1 is installed at /opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg and every named filter is present: loudnorm, silencedetect, silenceremove, astats, highpass, afftdn, arnndn, areverse, anlmdn, dynaudnorm.

The no-libsoxr claim is correct: `ffmpeg -version | grep -c libsoxr` returns 0, and the build configuration confirms no --enable-libsoxr. Any aresample=...:resampler=soxr recipe will fail; plain -ar is the right call.

The silenceremove stop_periods trap is real and I reproduced it independently. On a 14.20 s test signal with a 1.5 s internal gap, adding stop_periods=1:stop_duration=0 truncated the output to 5.18 s; the areverse-sandwich idiom produced 12.66 s with the internal pause intact — matching the plan's own 12.66 s figure.

The A1/A3/A4 command syntax is valid and runs. `-ss 612 -to 626` placed before -i is interpreted on the input timeline and yields exactly a 14 s window (I confirmed time=00:00:14.00). The A4 render produces a valid pcm_s16le mono 24 kHz file.
audioseal is real: PyPI 0.2.0, MIT licensed, py3-none-any wheel, requires torch>=1.13.0, source at github.com/facebookresearch/audioseal.
c2pa-python is real and Mac-native: 0.37.10 is the current version and the release includes a macosx_11_0_arm64 wheel, so no cmake is needed.

The AudioSeal macOS silent-failure incident is real and accurately quoted. The VoiceStudio v0.5.1 release notes exist and state that AudioSeal's lazy torch.compile sent the first embed into Inductor C++ codegen, failed on macOS toolchains, and "shipped the audio unmarked after a 30-40s wait." The plan's mandatory embed-then-detect startup self-test is well founded.

The Qwen3-TTS reference guidance is accurately characterized: 3 s minimum, 10-15 s recommended, quality plateaus then degrades past ~15 s, ref_text optional but raises speaker similarity from ~0.75 to ~0.89, x-vector-only mode available.
The NO FAKES Act summary is accurate and correctly hedged: S.4591, introduced May 20 2026, advanced by the Senate Judiciary Committee by voice vote June 18 2026, still a bill and not law.

Reynolds v. Reynolds (Ariz. Ct. App., April 24 2014) is a real case and is correctly described: it recognized a common-law right of publicity that is descendible, survives death, is not limited to celebrities, need not be exploited during life, and distinguishes commercial from First-Amendment-protected expressive use.

The legal section's overall posture is appropriately hedged. Every claim carries NOT LEGAL ADVICE, the Arizona domicile inference is explicitly flagged as an inference needing a lawyer, and the NO FAKES drafting ambiguity about whether pure production is reachable is honestly surfaced rather than resolved in the plan's favor.

The B6 structural finding is correct and is the most valuable insight in the plan. build_session_update at orchestrator.py:69-77 does set `"instructions": persona_text` with no wrapping, _apply_persona at :343 rebuilds it on every swap, and :476-479 exposes swapping to the browser. Prepending a GUARDRAIL_PREAMBLE constant at :77 is the right fix and is a two-line change.

config.py's persona wiring is as described: ref_wav existence-checked, ref_text hard-required when ref_wav is present (exits with 缺少 ref_text), and a persona must declare either ref_wav or voice_control. args.py passes --qwen3_tts_ref_audio / --qwen3_tts_ref_text through to the upstream CLI.

The voice-DESIGN alternative is genuinely first-class in this codebase, not a hack: personas/mojingnvwu.md carries voice_control plus a pinned voice_seed: 7, config.py accepts voice_control in place of ref_wav, and args.py only sends clone material when ref_wav is declared. The recommendation to put cloned-vs-designed to the user before any asset work is the strongest judgment call in the plan.

api.deepseek.com is indeed the only outbound host across web/, voxemw/ and configs/ (configs/assistant.yaml:43 and assistant-4090.yaml:20), and configs/assistant.yaml does set browser_ice_servers: [] with an explicit host-candidate comment.
`say -v Samantha` is available on this machine (184 voices installed), so the B2 pre-render command will work as written.

The C2PA findings — three signing gotchas, ~13 KB sidecar overhead with bit-identical PCM, and manifest destruction on re-encode — are internally consistent and the conclusion drawn from them (C2PA labels an intact file, AudioSeal survives transcoding, so layer them; and drop C2PA entirely if nothing is exported) is sound.
The recommendations to skip the talking-head renderer and to record only the user's own microphone track are both correct and well argued, and both reduce risk and cost simultaneously.

The risk section's framing that drift, not law, is the real hazard — and that an ungrounded persona is worse at debate practice as well as less defensible — is the right diagnosis. It is precisely because this is right that B8's infeasibility is fatal rather than cosmetic.
